basis: By its own terms the order performs one act: it takes the named lands out of a military or naval reservation (restoring them, relinquishing them to a territorial or Philippine government, or placing them under the Interior Department for disposal under the Act of July 5, 1884). The act was complete when the order issued; later disposal of the lands proceeds under the statute and the land laws, not under a continuing command of the order (coordinator ruling P1).
gaps: A later order could vacate a transfer to the Interior Department before disposal (EO 1011, EO 2377, EO 2563 and EO 636 did so for EO 803, EO 1422, EO 1279 and EO 372-B); a vacated transfer is ended by the vacating order (branches C09, C16, C23, C24), and the doctrine detects vacatur only where the vacating order is a member of this family. EO 3574 (Fort Davis) is decided by PLO 1712 on its own branch (P22).
Regex screens on the text decide that no reversion, retained right, redefinition or re-reservation is present; scan-OCR texts may hide such a clause.

BLM treated some Alaska transfers under the 1884 Act as continuing withdrawals: PLO 1712 (1958-08-07, held BLM table) revokes EO 3574 'entirely' and EO 7049 (four post cemeteries placed under Interior in 1935, on this branch) 'in part'. Under ruling P1 the transfer is spent on issue and the lead stands; if the owner reads such transfers as withdrawals pending disposal, Alaska members on this branch need the instrument that ended the withdrawal, and EO 7049's other tracts would be open.

Held later edges that act on the land after the order's date do not revive the spent act: EO 477 (1906) redefined the Fort Bayard reservation 'as modified by' EO 341-A; EO 5132 (1929) restored another parcel of the Hawaii Arsenal reservation that EO 3080 had also reduced; EO 4131 (1925) recites the Nulato right-of-way 'turned over to the Department of the Interior' by EO 3418. Each is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end) and leaves the lead unchanged.
source S-1884 (Act of July 5, 1884, ch. 214, sec. 1, 23 Stat. 103) is not yet held

basis: A lighthouse reservation continues until revoked by order or PLO, or until the station is conveyed; the 1939 transfer of the Bureau of Lighthouses to the Coast Guard and transfers of jurisdiction (for example EO 6896 moving San Miguel and Prince Islands to the Navy) continue it. Many such reservations were revoked by PLOs after 1947, station by station; none is held for this member.
gaps: Two held later edges are flagged by the engine as ending edges on this persistence-kind open lead; neither is a full end: PLO 1724 (1958) revokes EO 431 ("EOs of ... Mar. 27, 1906") only "in part" per the BLM table; PLO 7391 (1999) revokes an Oregon power-site order of November 14, 1917 (Power Site Reserve No. 658), a date collision with EO 2755, not EO 2755 itself.

Search the BLM PLO tables (held) and Federal Register for a PLO naming the order by number or date; the 1867-1906 and Alaska multi-site orders (for example EO 4257, revoked in part by six PLOs 1960-1994) need site-by-site review.

Later held BLM headings show partial revocations only: PLO 7583 (2003) of the Ediz Hook Lighthouse Reservation (reduced by EO 2646), and PLO 7723 (2008) of lighthouse withdrawals for Channel Islands National Park, which may reach the San Miguel, Prince and Santa Barbara Island orders (EO 1066, 2750, 347B, 6896); which lands they released is not identified in a held copy.
Light stations conveyed under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act (2000) or surplus-property law end by deed; GSA and NPS conveyance lists are not held.

basis: A refuge reservation continues until revoked; renaming (1940) and transfer to Interior (1939) continue it; if the area was in the Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps it until Congress acts (subject to the statute's exceptions for acquired-land disposals, exchanges and cooperative agreements), and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) bars the Secretary from revoking a withdrawal that added lands to the System before October 21, 1976. Whether the order's lands were still reserved in 1975 is not shown by the fields held.
gaps: Needed: evidence that the order's area was in the Refuge System on or after 1975-01-01 (FWS Annual Report of Lands for 1975 and the current year, matched to the order by a reviewed crosswalk) or a PLO revoking it.

Several such orders were revoked in part by PLOs (EO 2446 by PLO 2291, EO 4519 by PLO 988, EO 7106 by PLO 4641 and amended by PLO 1511, EO 7489 by PLO 3385); a partial revocation leaves the order in force as amended.

A held edge on EO 923 (Key West Reservation, 1908) from EO 10383 (1952) is a misresolution: EO 10383 restores lands set aside by 'Executive Order No. 923 of January 30, 1941, of the Governor of the Territory of Hawaii', not this order.

basis: The order's held text names a tribe listed in IRA sec. 13 and places it in Oklahoma; sec. 13 provides that sec. 2 "shall not apply" to those tribes, so the statute did not continue the period this order fixed, and the Act of June 15, 1935 (which reaches only reservations that voted to exclude themselves under sec. 18, a section sec. 13 also makes inapplicable) does not reach it either. The Oklahoma Indian Welfare Act of June 26, 1936 does not by its words extend, continue or reimpose trust periods on existing allotments. The order therefore ended by its own terms at the end of its stated period; later Oklahoma extensions (EO 6926, 7206, 7464 and the later general orders) are separate executive orders with their own lifecycles.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). basis: The order fixed a trust period that was still running on 1934-06-18 on a reservation that the held text does not place among the sec. 13 Oklahoma tribes. IRA sec. 2 by its words extended and continued "the existing periods of trust placed upon any Indian lands" until Congress directs otherwise, and this order's operative content is such a period; its stated end is therefore not a sound TERM end (P8). Whether the period, and with it the order's operative effect, was in force on 2026-10-14 depends on the reservation's IRA status and on the current state of the trust lands. The Act's sec. 3(i) "deemed" these orders "to have extended trust periods" that would otherwise have expired in 1927, 1932 or 1933; that describes their past extension and is not a current predicate. EO 5768 and 5953 also cover reservations of sec. 13 Oklahoma tribes (Otoe, Eastern Shawnee, Kiowa) alongside IRA reservations, so the order as a whole cannot be decided by either rule.
gaps: Whether the reservation came under the IRA or voted to exclude itself under sec. 18 (the election results are not held); if it excluded itself, the Act of June 15, 1935 reaches only periods not extended past 1936-12-31, and this order's own stated end may then stand.
A current record of the trust lands on 2026-10-14 (25 U.S.C. 5102 for IRA reservations; BIA land title records), with no later Act of Congress ending the trust, such as a termination act.
IRA sec. 2 (48 Stat. 984), 25 U.S.C. 5102 and the Act of June 15, 1935 are read only on the web, not held.
EO 5768 is dated December 30, 1931 in its held text and "December 10, 1931" in the Act.

basis: A refuge reservation continues until revoked; renaming (1940) and transfer to Interior (1939) continue it; if the area was in the Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps it until Congress acts (subject to the statute's exceptions for acquired-land disposals, exchanges and cooperative agreements), and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) bars the Secretary from revoking a withdrawal that added lands to the System before October 21, 1976. Whether the order's lands were still reserved in 1975 is not shown by the fields held.
gaps: Needed: evidence that the order's area was in the Refuge System on or after 1975-01-01 (FWS Annual Report of Lands for 1975 and the current year, matched to the order by a reviewed crosswalk) or a PLO revoking it.

Several such orders were revoked in part by PLOs (EO 2446 by PLO 2291, EO 4519 by PLO 988, EO 7106 by PLO 4641 and amended by PLO 1511, EO 7489 by PLO 3385); a partial revocation leaves the order in force as amended.

A held edge on EO 923 (Key West Reservation, 1908) from EO 10383 (1952) is a misresolution: EO 10383 restores lands set aside by 'Executive Order No. 923 of January 30, 1941, of the Governor of the Territory of Hawaii', not this order.

basis: The member's own text only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; its text merged into those rules on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent rules were expressly revoked by EO 89 ('revokes all others') on May 6, 1896.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

gaps: The Forest Service chronological record mapping this order to the named forest's later actions (consolidation, renaming, redescription), with the text of each later instrument to test whether it names this order or expressly redescribes the whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions.

basis: A refuge reservation continues until revoked; renaming (1940) and transfer to Interior (1939) continue it; if the area was in the Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps it until Congress acts (subject to the statute's exceptions for acquired-land disposals, exchanges and cooperative agreements), and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) bars the Secretary from revoking a withdrawal that added lands to the System before October 21, 1976. Whether the order's lands were still reserved in 1975 is not shown by the fields held.
gaps: Needed: evidence that the order's area was in the Refuge System on or after 1975-01-01 (FWS Annual Report of Lands for 1975 and the current year, matched to the order by a reviewed crosswalk) or a PLO revoking it.

Several such orders were revoked in part by PLOs (EO 2446 by PLO 2291, EO 4519 by PLO 988, EO 7106 by PLO 4641 and amended by PLO 1511, EO 7489 by PLO 3385); a partial revocation leaves the order in force as amended.

A held edge on EO 923 (Key West Reservation, 1908) from EO 10383 (1952) is a misresolution: EO 10383 restores lands set aside by 'Executive Order No. 923 of January 30, 1941, of the Governor of the Territory of Hawaii', not this order.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.
gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.

EO 2281 (Alabama military lands, 1915-12-06) carries held revocation edges from EO 5590 (1931), which revokes in part 'Executive order of December 6, 1915, creating Petroleum Reserve No. 40, Montana No. 1', a different order of the same date; the edge does not reach EO 2281. The engine flags it (persistence_lead_but_held_ending_edge); the lead stays open.

basis: 19 CFR 101.3(b)(1) (April 1, 2025 edition) cites this executive order beside a port that exists today, as the order that created the port or fixed its limits; the regulation thus relies on the order's operative effect. A citation shows the regulation relies on the order; it does not show that every clause of a multi-clause order survives. Later Treasury Decisions cited beside the same port (for example T.D. 78-130 for Bar Harbor) may have redrawn part of the limits.

The match to 19 CFR 101.3 is by executive order number; for EO 5770 and EO 6284 the regulation's date (Dec. 31, 1931; Sept. 13, 1933) differs by a few days from the member date (1931-12-30; 1933-09-18) and should be checked against the order's official text.

XI); but U.S. military forces kept using defense sites under the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV, a new instrument that excepts that property from the transfer (coordinator ruling P5). The Treaty, and with it every U.S. right to use areas in the former Zone, terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (art. II: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999'). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 (held) treats 'Canal Zone' thereafter as the areas in the Republic of Panama made available under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)) but contains no words ending these reservations earlier.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. basis: The order fixed a trust period that was still running on 1934-06-18 on a reservation that the held text does not place among the sec. 13 Oklahoma tribes. IRA sec. 2 by its words extended and continued "the existing periods of trust placed upon any Indian lands" until Congress directs otherwise, and this order's operative content is such a period; its stated end is therefore not a sound TERM end (P8). Whether the period, and with it the order's operative effect, was in force on 2026-10-14 depends on the reservation's IRA status and on the current state of the trust lands. The Act's sec. 3(i) "deemed" these orders "to have extended trust periods" that would otherwise have expired in 1927, 1932 or 1933; that describes their past extension and is not a current predicate. EO 5768 and 5953 also cover reservations of sec. 13 Oklahoma tribes (Otoe, Eastern Shawnee, Kiowa) alongside IRA reservations, so the order as a whole cannot be decided by either rule.
gaps: Whether the reservation came under the IRA or voted to exclude itself under sec. 18 (the election results are not held); if it excluded itself, the Act of June 15, 1935 reaches only periods not extended past 1936-12-31, and this order's own stated end may then stand.
A current record of the trust lands on 2026-10-14 (25 U.S.C. 5102 for IRA reservations; BIA land title records), with no later Act of Congress ending the trust, such as a termination act.
IRA sec. 2 (48 Stat. 984), 25 U.S.C. 5102 and the Act of June 15, 1935 are read only on the web, not held.
EO 5768 is dated December 30, 1931 in its held text and "December 10, 1931" in the Act.

basis: The exemption can apply only to the persons named, each of whom had reached (or reached that month) a statutory retirement age, the lowest of which is 62 (S6, S7). With a minimum age of 61, every named person died no later than order date - 61 years + 122 years 164 days (at the latest 1994-06-18 for the members on this branch). The result holds for any minimum age of 29 or more (the latest member is dated January 5, 1933).

date.basis: latest member 1933-01-05 minus 61 years plus 122 years 164 days

gaps: The bound rests on the longest verified human life (S1, held only on the web until acquired).
Each order names several persons; the order is spent only when every person's exemption has ended, and the bound covers all of them because each reached retirement age.
Later serial exemptions of the same persons (EO 5873, 5875 for EO 5896) do not affect the bound.

basis: The order is an operative act on land whose forest designation persists, not a pure textual amendment, so ruling P2 does not reach it; it ends only when a later order or statute names it or expressly redescribes the forest's whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions, and no such instrument is held.
gaps: The Forest Service chronological record mapping this order to the named forest's later actions (consolidation, renaming, redescription), with the text of each later instrument to test whether it names this order or expressly redescribes the whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions.
For a persistence lead: the current Land Areas Report showing the forest or name on 2026-10-14. 16 U.S.C. 1609(a) is context only.

Where the forest the order constituted was later abolished or merged by name but the order also assigned land to another forest (for example EO 870, Holy Cross and Leadville, Holy Cross abolished by PLO 263; EO 801, Pocatello and Cache, Pocatello merged by EO 2179), ruling P7 does not reach it and the lead stays open.

basis: 19 CFR 101.3(b)(1) (April 1, 2025 edition) cites this executive order beside a port that exists today, as the order that created the port or fixed its limits; the regulation thus relies on the order's operative effect. Where the order also abolished other ports, those provisions were single acts already performed; the lead is that the order is in force at least in the provision the regulation cites.
gaps: The held CFR edition is revised as of April 1, 2025, 18 months before the cutoff; the eCFR amendment history (S2, read on the web, not held) shows no amendment of 101.3 after 2023-11-16. Acquire the eCFR text as of 2026-10-14 to close the gap.

A citation shows the regulation relies on the order; it does not show that every clause of a multi-clause order survives. Later Treasury Decisions cited beside the same port (for example T.D. 78-130 for Bar Harbor) may have redrawn part of the limits.

The match to 19 CFR 101.3 is by executive order number; for EO 5770 and EO 6284 the regulation's date (Dec. 31, 1931; Sept. 13, 1933) differs by a few days from the member date (1931-12-30; 1933-09-18) and should be checked against the order's official text.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.
gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.

EO 2281 (Alabama military lands, 1915-12-06) carries held revocation edges from EO 5590 (1931), which revokes in part 'Executive order of December 6, 1915, creating Petroleum Reserve No. 40, Montana No. 1', a different order of the same date; the edge does not reach EO 2281. The engine flags it (persistence_lead_but_held_ending_edge); the lead stays open.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.
gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.

EO 2281 (Alabama military lands, 1915-12-06) carries held revocation edges from EO 5590 (1931), which revokes in part 'Executive order of December 6, 1915, creating Petroleum Reserve No. 40, Montana No. 1', a different order of the same date; the edge does not reach EO 2281. The engine flags it (persistence_lead_but_held_ending_edge); the lead stays open.

basis: The President set these reservations apart within the Canal Zone, or on adjacent lands whose use the 1903 Isthmian Canal Convention granted. The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979, terminated and superseded the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)(a)), and returned plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone to Panama (art. XI); but U.S. military forces kept using defense sites under the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV, a new instrument that excepts that property from the transfer (coordinator ruling P5). The Treaty, and with it every U.S. right to use areas in the former Zone, terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (art. II: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999'). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 (held) treats 'Canal Zone' thereafter as the areas in the Republic of Panama made available under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)) but contains no words ending these reservations earlier.

date.basis: termination of the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 at noon on 1999-12-31 (art. II); earlier if a later order superseded or rescinded the member

gaps: The Panama Canal Treaty (1280 U.N.T.S. No. 21086) and the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV are not held; the Treaty was read on the web only. Acquire both.

A member whose land passed to Panama on October 1, 1979 (outside the defense sites) ended then; identifying those needs the Article IV agreement's annexes. Sec. 1504(a)(1) of the Panama Canal Act (held, 93 Stat. 488) authorized the Secretary of State to convey to Panama, on the Treaty's entry into force, property in the former Zone 'which is not within the land and water areas the use of which is made available to the United States'.
source S-PCT (Panama Canal Treaty, signed Sept. 7, 1977, arts. I, II, IV, XI, 33 U.S.T. 39, T.I.A.S. No. 10030, 1280 U.N.T.S. No. 21086; in force Oct. 1, 1979) is not yet held

basis: The member's own text only amends a numbered Civil Service Rule or Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); its text merged into EO 209 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent's lead (EO 209) is open.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

disclosed earlier candidate end for the parent EO 209: EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01; under ruling P3 a restatement that does not name EO 209 does not end it, so EO 209's own lead is open

thirteen decided members carry a year-only census date (on B14: EO 508, 689, 933, 1127, 1128, 1247, 1408, 1829, 2700, 2701, 3908A and 4507; on B15: EO 3170), so their lead date is a year; several held texts give the day (EO 689: September 23, 1907; EO 933: September 3, 1908)

basis: The member's own text only amends a numbered Civil Service Rule or Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); its text merged into EO 209 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent's lead (EO 209) is open.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

disclosed earlier candidate end for the parent EO 209: EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01; under ruling P3 a restatement that does not name EO 209 does not end it, so EO 209's own lead is open

basis: The member's own text only amends a numbered Civil Service Rule or Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); its text merged into EO 209 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent's lead (EO 209) is open.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

disclosed earlier candidate end for the parent EO 209: EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01; under ruling P3 a restatement that does not name EO 209 does not end it, so EO 209's own lead is open

basis: The order only amends or adds to paragraphs of presidentially prescribed regulations (the Consular Regulations of 1896, the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers of 1897 or 1927, the Tariff of Consular Fees). Coordinator ruling P2 covers amendments of such regulations as well as of numbered orders: the order merges into the parent on issue. The parent's later history is held at least in part: EO 5642, effective July 1, 1931, cancels and replaces Article I ('The Consular Branch of the Foreign Service'), Article II ('Retirement of Foreign Service Officers'), sections 465-473 (leave of absence) and Article XXV ('Compensation of Consular Officers') of the Consular Regulations, and the parts of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers covering the same subjects. That reaches the text inserted by at least EO 5127 (sections 465, 467), EO 5126 (Instructions VI-5) and parts of EO 3354 (Article I paragraphs) and EO 3902 and EO 1926 (paragraphs 491-492); the list is not exhaustive and changes no lead.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent (the regulations or order amended) until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

EO 610 is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end): edge SH-bdbb6b2087da records that EO 2022 (1914) amends EO 610, i.e. it rewrites paragraphs 159-160 of the Consular Regulations and the Instructions that EO 610 had amended. Under P2 that is a later event of the parent regulations, not a command of EO 610.

basis: The order only amends or adds to paragraphs of presidentially prescribed regulations (the Consular Regulations of 1896, the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers of 1897 or 1927, the Tariff of Consular Fees). Coordinator ruling P2 covers amendments of such regulations as well as of numbered orders: the order merges into the parent on issue. The parent's later history is held at least in part: EO 5642, effective July 1, 1931, cancels and replaces Article I ('The Consular Branch of the Foreign Service'), Article II ('Retirement of Foreign Service Officers'), sections 465-473 (leave of absence) and Article XXV ('Compensation of Consular Officers') of the Consular Regulations, and the parts of the Instructions to Diplomatic Officers covering the same subjects. That reaches the text inserted by at least EO 5127 (sections 465, 467), EO 5126 (Instructions VI-5) and parts of EO 3354 (Article I paragraphs) and EO 3902 and EO 1926 (paragraphs 491-492); the list is not exhaustive and changes no lead.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent (the regulations or order amended) until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

EO 610 is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end): edge SH-bdbb6b2087da records that EO 2022 (1914) amends EO 610, i.e. it rewrites paragraphs 159-160 of the Consular Regulations and the Instructions that EO 610 had amended. Under P2 that is a later event of the parent regulations, not a command of EO 610.

Other held edges on B21 members are number collisions with different orders and are not used: EO 1161 (PLO 5757 revokes a Nevada land order of Feb. 17, 1903), EO 1926 (PLO 1178, partial), EO 2462 (EO 9804, partial: an order of Sept. 29, 1916 on the Employees' Compensation Act), EO 422 (EO 9951: a Hawaii order of July 23, 1930).

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.
gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.

EO 2281 (Alabama military lands, 1915-12-06) carries held revocation edges from EO 5590 (1931), which revokes in part 'Executive order of December 6, 1915, creating Petroleum Reserve No. 40, Montana No. 1', a different order of the same date; the edge does not reach EO 2281. The engine flags it (persistence_lead_but_held_ending_edge); the lead stays open.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: The member's own text only amends a numbered Civil Service Rule or Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); its text merged into EO 209 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent's lead (EO 209) is open.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

disclosed earlier candidate end for the parent EO 209: EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01; under ruling P3 a restatement that does not name EO 209 does not end it, so EO 209's own lead is open

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

date.basis: EO 7076; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended by S.J. Res. 113 sec. 1

gaps: EO 7076 is held only as a mirror transcription.
Orders citing Title I 'and otherwise' may rest partly on unnamed general authority; EO 7076 reaches them because they were issued under Title I.
The authority-clause test is a text pattern: it reads the 350 characters after 'authority vested in me'.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: The order fixed a trust period that was still running on 1934-06-18 on a reservation that the held text does not place among the sec. 13 Oklahoma tribes. IRA sec. 2 by its words extended and continued "the existing periods of trust placed upon any Indian lands" until Congress directs otherwise, and this order's operative content is such a period; its stated end is therefore not a sound TERM end (P8). Whether the period, and with it the order's operative effect, was in force on 2026-10-14 depends on the reservation's IRA status and on the current state of the trust lands.
gaps: Whether the reservation came under the IRA or voted to exclude itself under sec. 18 (the election results are not held); if it excluded itself, the Act of June 15, 1935 reaches only periods not extended past 1936-12-31, and this order's own stated end may then stand.
A current record of the trust lands on 2026-10-14 (25 U.S.C. 5102 for IRA reservations; BIA land title records), with no later Act of Congress ending the trust, such as a termination act.
IRA sec. 2 (48 Stat. 984), 25 U.S.C. 5102 and the Act of June 15, 1935 are read only on the web, not held.
Crow (EO 5301): the Act of April 11, 1940 also reimposed Crow periods that expired before its approval, a second statute reaching this period.
Yakima (EO 4168, 5746): the Act of May 27, 1937 also reimposed Yakima periods expired before its approval.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: By its own terms the order performs one act: it takes the named lands out of a military or naval reservation (restoring them, relinquishing them to a territorial or Philippine government, or placing them under the Interior Department for disposal under the Act of July 5, 1884). The act was complete when the order issued; later disposal of the lands proceeds under the statute and the land laws, not under a continuing command of the order (coordinator ruling P1).
gaps: A later order could vacate a transfer to the Interior Department before disposal (EO 1011, EO 2377, EO 2563 and EO 636 did so for EO 803, EO 1422, EO 1279 and EO 372-B); a vacated transfer is ended by the vacating order (branches C09, C16, C23, C24), and the doctrine detects vacatur only where the vacating order is a member of this family. EO 3574 (Fort Davis) is decided by PLO 1712 on its own branch (P22).
Regex screens on the text decide that no reversion, retained right, redefinition or re-reservation is present; scan-OCR texts may hide such a clause.

BLM treated some Alaska transfers under the 1884 Act as continuing withdrawals: PLO 1712 (1958-08-07, held BLM table) revokes EO 3574 'entirely' and EO 7049 (four post cemeteries placed under Interior in 1935, on this branch) 'in part'. basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

date.basis: EO 7076; NIRA sec. 2(c) as amended by S.J. Res. 113 sec. 1

gaps: EO 7076 is held only as a mirror transcription.
Orders citing Title I 'and otherwise' may rest partly on unnamed general authority; EO 7076 reaches them because they were issued under Title I.
The authority-clause test is a text pattern: it reads the 350 characters after 'authority vested in me'.

gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

disclosed earlier candidate end for the parent EO 209: EO 7915 and EO 8043 restated the whole text of the rules and of Schedules A and B effective 1939-02-01; under ruling P3 a restatement that does not name EO 209 does not end it, so EO 209's own lead is open

basis: The order opens returns to a named committee, official or class of officers (or generally under Treasury rules) and states no period or end. gaps: Disclosed earlier candidate end: 1977-01-01, when Tax Reform Act of 1976 sec. 1202 (90 Stat. 1667, 1672, 1688; held) made returns confidential except as Title 26 authorizes and left no inspection upon order of the President; under P3 it does not end the member because it does not name it or an expressly described class that includes it.

For grants to a congressional committee under a resolution named in the text (EO 6241, 6712, 6742, 7039, 7097, 7115, 7158, 7322, 7350, 7411, 7483): the end of the committee's authority under its resolution, from the Journal or Congressional Record; a House resolution's authority ending with its Congress would need a held source (House rules or precedents).

EO 3595 (two firms' returns opened to 'Honorable Joseph W. Fordney, Chairman of the Ways & Means Committee', or a member he designates) and EO 6603A (returns opened to the House Committee on Naval Affairs) name no resolution: each grant runs to a standing committee, or its named chairman, and its end depends on that committee's inquiry or the chairman's tenure, which no held source fixes.

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it
a compiled transcription can run into a neighbouring order

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

The authority-clause test is a text pattern: it reads the 350 characters after 'authority vested in me'.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: The member's own text only amends a numbered Civil Service Rule or Schedule A or B of the 1903 rules (EO 209); its text merged into EO 209 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent's lead (EO 209) is open.

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: A lighthouse reservation continues until revoked by order or PLO, or until the station is conveyed; the 1939 transfer of the Bureau of Lighthouses to the Coast Guard and transfers of jurisdiction (for example EO 6896 moving San Miguel and Prince Islands to the Navy) continue it. Many such reservations were revoked by PLOs after 1947, station by station; none is held for this member.
gaps: Two held later edges are flagged by the engine as ending edges on this persistence-kind open lead; neither is a full end: PLO 1724 (1958) revokes EO 431 ("EOs of ... Mar. 27, 1906") only "in part" per the BLM table; PLO 7391 (1999) revokes an Oregon power-site order of November 14, 1917 (Power Site Reserve No. 658), a date collision with EO 2755, not EO 2755 itself.

Search the BLM PLO tables (held) and Federal Register for a PLO naming the order by number or date; the 1867-1906 and Alaska multi-site orders (for example EO 4257, revoked in part by six PLOs 1960-1994) need site-by-site review.

Later held BLM headings show partial revocations only: PLO 7583 (2003) of the Ediz Hook Lighthouse Reservation (reduced by EO 2646), and PLO 7723 (2008) of lighthouse withdrawals for Channel Islands National Park, which may reach the San Miguel, Prince and Santa Barbara Island orders (EO 1066, 2750, 347B, 6896); which lands they released is not identified in a held copy.
Light stations conveyed under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act (2000) or surplus-property law end by deed; GSA and NPS conveyance lists are not held.

basis: Words that reach the reservation: section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directs the surrender of 'all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', states that the United States 'hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised' over the territory; and Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946) withdraws and surrenders all such rights 'except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases, and the right incident thereto, as the United States of America, by agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, may deem necessary to retain'. The agreement so made, the Military Bases Agreement in force March 26, 1947, retains the use of the bases listed in Annex A (and Annex B on necessity), which do not include this member's place; keeps the Port of Manila reservation (art. XXI(2)); and keeps only one other class outside the bases: 'temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases ... for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years', with any extension fixed by agreement, barred for the City of Manila, and one that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years' (art. XXI(1)). Member test: the reservation lies in the Philippine Islands, is an Army reservation, and its place is neither an Annex A or B base nor the Port of Manila reservation. Whether U.S. forces still occupied an installation on this member's land in 1947 is not known from the fields held; if they did, art. XXI(1) let them stay at most two years plus an extension of at most three years, so the U.S. right over the land ended no later than five years after the agreement took effect.

date.basis: No later than the outer limit of art. XXI(1) of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement: two years plus an extension that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years', counted from the agreement's entry into force on 1947-03-26 (on the narrower reading that three years is the whole period, 1950-03-26; for temporary installations within the City of Manila, where no extension was allowed, 1949-03-26). July 4, 1946 (Proclamation 2695) or October 22, 1946 (Treaty art. I) for a member whose land held no U.S. installation in 1947; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands.

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) and the Military Bases Agreement (61 Stat. 4019; 43 U.N.T.S. No. 673) are read on the web only; acquire them.

Note V of the 1947 agreement, in full: 'I have the honor to state, in signing the Agreement of March 14, 1947, Between the United States of America and the Republic of the Philippines Concerning Military Bases, the understanding of my Government that the question of the adjustment of any rights and titles held by the United States pursuant to the provisions of the Act of Congress of March 24, 1934 (48 Stat. 456) as amended, specifically Section 10(b) thereof, the Joint Resolution of the Congress of June 29, 1944, and the Act of Congress of July 3, 1946, and Treaties and Agreements heretofore entered into between the United States and the Philippines, to real property in any of the bases covered by the aforementioned Agreement or any naval reservations or fueling stations not so covered is reserved and will be settled subsequently in accordance with the terms of the Acts and Joint Resolution of the Congress mentioned above.' (61 Stat. 4033; Note VI, the Philippine reply, concurs 'without conceding the existence of any rights or titles to the real property therein referred to'.) Note V reserves title questions for the bases and for naval reservations outside them (the latter routed to B20n); it does not reserve the possession and control of an Army reservation outside the bases, which Article I surrendered. Section 5 of the 1934 Act likewise kept designated reservation lands out of the 1935 grant to the Commonwealth. Any U.S. title that outlasted the surrender is a property question disclosed here, not a continuation of the reservation.

The joint resolution of June 29, 1944 (58 Stat. 626) is read on the web only; which bases, if any, the President withheld under it before July 4, 1946 is not established in the sources held. A withheld base is retained only through the 1947 agreement, so the interval's bound covers it.

Which members' lands held U.S. temporary installations in March 1947 is not known; the interval's upper bound assumes the widest reading of art. XXI(1). A later agreement extending a temporary installation beyond the art. XXI(1) limit would be a new instrument; none is held.

For Manila members: Proclamation 2694 of July 3, 1946 (closing part on the held 60 Stat. 1352 page; number, title and authority read on the Truman Library copy; opening page not verified) designated nine Manila properties for U.S. diplomatic and consular establishments under section 10 of the 1934 Act as amended in 1939; any U.S. use of such a property rests on that proclamation, not on a military reservation order.

EO 1437 (Regan Barracks target range) was placed under the Government of the Philippine Islands by EO 3086 of 1919, 'subject to such reimbursement and reservations as may be prescribed by the Secretary of War'; because of that proviso the class interval is kept. EO 1628 (Fort Pikit and Fort Reina Regente) appears to have been transferred by EO 3056 of 1919-03-03 (see branch C28).

EO 985 carries a held 'amendment' edge from EO 10069 (1949), which amends 'Executive Order No. 985 of November 25, 1946' on travel expenses; that is a different order (a misprint of the number), so the edge does not act on EO 985. The engine flags it (acted_on_after_lead_end).
The order's day and month are not in MEMBERS (date '1907'); the held text or the WPA list would give the exact date.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

basis: EO 7076 ordered 'that all existing Executive Orders heretofore issued under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act be, and they are, hereby amended so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936'. Member test: the member's own text names a Title I power (Title I, a code of fair competition, section 9(c) or its petroleum words, the President's Reemployment Agreement, section 2(b) or 10(a)); it is dated before June 15, 1935; its authority clause (the words following 'authority vested in me') cites no other statute, and it allocates no funds and charters no corporation. Mentions of other statutes outside the authority clause (a recital or a descriptive clause) do not exclude a member. It is therefore an existing order issued under Title I, and EO 7076 fixed April 1, 1936 as the last day of its operation. Earlier candidate ends are disclosed, not applied: the June 14, 1935 repeal of the code provisions (S.J. Res. 113 sec. 2) for code-dependent commands, and exhaustion on issue for denials and dismissals. Schechter and Panama Refining are validity notes, not ends.

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

By its own terms the order ends on that vote if the vote accepted the Act, and otherwise at the end of its stated period (1945-1946). The sec. 18 election results are not held, so the doctrine does not choose between the two ends.
gaps: The sec. 18 election result and date for the Spokane, Klamath (Oregon), Colville and Crow reservations (Interior records; Haas, Ten Years of Tribal Government under I.R.A., 1947). Either result ends the order before the cutoff unless a statute continued its period: for Crow, the Act of April 11, 1940 reimposes only periods that had expired before its approval (this order's had not).
IRA sec. 2 (48 Stat. 984), 25 U.S.C. 5102 and the Act of June 15, 1935 are read only on the web, not held.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. basis: Each order extends the trust periods expiring during 1935 for ten years from expiry, "subject to the provisions of the act of June 18, 1934", and provides that if the reservation's adult Indians vote at the sec. 18 election to apply the Act, "this order shall thereafter cease to be of force and effect". The sec. 18 election results are not held, so the doctrine does not choose between the two ends.

basis: By its own terms the order performs one act: it takes the named lands out of a military or naval reservation (restoring them, relinquishing them to a territorial or Philippine government, or placing them under the Interior Department for disposal under the Act of July 5, 1884). The act was complete when the order issued; later disposal of the lands proceeds under the statute and the land laws, not under a continuing command of the order (coordinator ruling P1).
gaps: A later order could vacate a transfer to the Interior Department before disposal (EO 1011, EO 2377, EO 2563 and EO 636 did so for EO 803, EO 1422, EO 1279 and EO 372-B); a vacated transfer is ended by the vacating order (branches C09, C16, C23, C24), and the doctrine detects vacatur only where the vacating order is a member of this family. EO 3574 (Fort Davis) is decided by PLO 1712 on its own branch (P22).
Regex screens on the text decide that no reversion, retained right, redefinition or re-reservation is present; scan-OCR texts may hide such a clause.

BLM treated some Alaska transfers under the 1884 Act as continuing withdrawals: PLO 1712 (1958-08-07, held BLM table) revokes EO 3574 'entirely' and EO 7049 (four post cemeteries placed under Interior in 1935, on this branch) 'in part'. Under ruling P1 the transfer is spent on issue and the lead stands; if the owner reads such transfers as withdrawals pending disposal, Alaska members on this branch need the instrument that ended the withdrawal, and EO 7049's other tracts would be open.

Held later edges that act on the land after the order's date do not revive the spent act: EO 477 (1906) redefined the Fort Bayard reservation 'as modified by' EO 341-A; EO 5132 (1929) restored another parcel of the Hawaii Arsenal reservation that EO 3080 had also reduced; EO 4131 (1925) recites the Nulato right-of-way 'turned over to the Department of the Interior' by EO 3418. Each is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end) and leaves the lead unchanged.
