only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: If the refuge was in the National Wildlife Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps the area in the System until Congress acts; but (a)(6) expressly does not preclude transfer or disposal of acquired lands under 668dd(a)(5) (which needs Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval), exchanges, or disposal under a cooperative agreement, and these orders reserve acquired lands. Persistence of the order therefore needs both a link from the order to a current refuge unit and evidence that its lands were not transferred, exchanged or disposed of under those exceptions; neither is held.
gaps: Needed: a reviewed crosswalk from each order to a current refuge unit in the FWS Annual Report of Lands (FY2024 Table 3 lists refuge names and acreage, not executive orders) or the refuge's FWS establishing-document file.
Needed: evidence that the order's acquired lands were not transferred, exchanged or disposed of under 668dd(a)(5), (b)(3) or a cooperative agreement, none of which needs an Act of Congress.
No held search shows a full revocation; absence of a found revocation is not evidence of persistence.

basis: A regulation order stands until revoked or superseded; the later instruments that replaced these series (later ration and passport orders, the Manuals for Courts-Martial, the Veterans' Benefits Act of 1957) are not held, and the 1957 Act carries a savings section for outstanding regulations (sec. 2307) whose terms must be read.

L. 85-56, 71 Stat. 83 (June 17, 1957), title XXII (beginning 71 Stat. 157) and title XXIII (beginning 71 Stat. 172), sec. 2307 'Outstanding rules, regulations, and orders' (page of sec. 2307 unverified); later passport and Army ration orders that state they supersede earlier ones.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: The order opens returns to a named committee, official or class of officers (or generally under Treasury rules) and states no period or end. Its own terms tie it to the named body, whose end is not in the text; the 1976 rewrite of 26 U.S.C. 6103 does not name the order or describe a class of orders (P3), so it is only a candidate end.
gaps: Disclosed earlier candidate end: 1977-01-01, when Tax Reform Act of 1976 sec. 1202 (90 Stat. 1667, 1672, 1688; held) made returns confidential except as Title 26 authorizes and left no inspection upon order of the President; under P3 it does not end the member because it does not name it or an expressly described class that includes it.

For grants to a congressional committee under a resolution named in the text (EO 6241, 6712, 6742, 7039, 7097, 7115, 7158, 7322, 7350, 7411, 7483): the end of the committee's authority under its resolution, from the Journal or Congressional Record; a House resolution's authority ending with its Congress would need a held source (House rules or precedents).

EO 3595 (two firms' returns opened to 'Honorable Joseph W. Fordney, Chairman of the Ways & Means Committee', or a member he designates) and EO 6603A (returns opened to the House Committee on Naval Affairs) name no resolution: each grant runs to a standing committee, or its named chairman, and its end depends on that committee's inquiry or the chairman's tenure, which no held source fixes.

For general orders under Treasury rules and standing orders for State officers (EO 1999, 2882A, 2934A, 3212, 3624, 3971A, 4078, 4416, 4940, 5321, 5647, 5824, 5970, 2130): a later order that supersedes them by number or by express class.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.
gaps: A yes needs a current predicate: a statute naming the reservation, or current BLM (MLRS/LR2000) withdrawal records or DoD real property records showing the order's lands still reserved under it. basis: The President set these reservations apart within the Canal Zone, or on adjacent lands whose use the 1903 Isthmian Canal Convention granted. The Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 entered into force on October 1, 1979, terminated and superseded the 1903 Convention (art. I(1)(a)), and returned plenary jurisdiction over the former Zone to Panama (art. XI); but U.S. military forces kept using defense sites under the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV, a new instrument that excepts that property from the transfer (coordinator ruling P5). The Treaty, and with it every U.S. right to use areas in the former Zone, terminated at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999 (art. II: 'This Treaty shall terminate at noon, Panama time, December 31, 1999'). The Panama Canal Act of 1979 (held) treats 'Canal Zone' thereafter as the areas in the Republic of Panama made available under the Treaty (sec. 3(b)(1)) but contains no words ending these reservations earlier.

date.basis: termination of the Panama Canal Treaty of 1977 at noon on 1999-12-31 (art. II); earlier if a later order superseded or rescinded the member

gaps: The Panama Canal Treaty (1280 U.N.T.S. No. 21086) and the Agreement in Implementation of Article IV are not held; the Treaty was read on the web only. Acquire both.

A member whose land passed to Panama on October 1, 1979 (outside the defense sites) ended then; identifying those needs the Article IV agreement's annexes. Sec. 1504(a)(1) of the Panama Canal Act (held, 93 Stat. 488) authorized the Secretary of State to convey to Panama, on the Treaty's entry into force, property in the former Zone 'which is not within the land and water areas the use of which is made available to the United States'.

basis: If the refuge was in the National Wildlife Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps the area in the System until Congress acts; but (a)(6) expressly does not preclude transfer or disposal of acquired lands under 668dd(a)(5) (which needs Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval), exchanges, or disposal under a cooperative agreement, and these orders reserve acquired lands. Needed: evidence that the order's acquired lands were not transferred, exchanged or disposed of under 668dd(a)(5), (b)(3) or a cooperative agreement, none of which needs an Act of Congress.
No held search shows a full revocation; absence of a found revocation is not evidence of persistence.

basis: The order opens returns to a named committee, official or class of officers (or generally under Treasury rules) and states no period or end. Its own terms tie it to the named body, whose end is not in the text; the 1976 rewrite of 26 U.S.C. 6103 does not name the order or describe a class of orders (P3), so it is only a candidate end.
gaps: Disclosed earlier candidate end: 1977-01-01, when Tax Reform Act of 1976 sec. 1202 (90 Stat. 1667, 1672, 1688; held) made returns confidential except as Title 26 authorizes and left no inspection upon order of the President; under P3 it does not end the member because it does not name it or an expressly described class that includes it.

For grants to a congressional committee under a resolution named in the text (EO 6241, 6712, 6742, 7039, 7097, 7115, 7158, 7322, 7350, 7411, 7483): the end of the committee's authority under its resolution, from the Journal or Congressional Record; a House resolution's authority ending with its Congress would need a held source (House rules or precedents).

basis: The member's operative content is U.S. supervision of the Islands' government (EO 2456 places 'all matters pertaining to the Government of the Philippine Islands' under the War Department and directs the Governor General's reports there; EO 7447 delegates to the High Commissioner the Commonwealth's extradition business). Section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directed the President to 'withdraw and surrender all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty then existing and exercised by the United States in and over the territory and people of the Philippine Islands', and Proclamation 2695 declared on July 4, 1946: 'The United States of America hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised by the United States of America in and over the territory and people of the Philippines'. For EO 7447, section 7 of the Act, under which the High Commissioner served, applies only 'Until the final and complete withdrawal of American sovereignty'. basis: By its own terms the order performs one act: it takes the named lands out of a military or naval reservation (restoring them, relinquishing them to a territorial or Philippine government, or placing them under the Interior Department for disposal under the Act of July 5, 1884). The act was complete when the order issued; later disposal of the lands proceeds under the statute and the land laws, not under a continuing command of the order (coordinator ruling P1).
gaps: A later order could vacate a transfer to the Interior Department before disposal (EO 1011, EO 2377, EO 2563 and EO 636 did so for EO 803, EO 1422, EO 1279 and EO 372-B); a vacated transfer is ended by the vacating order (branches C09, C16, C23, C24), and the doctrine detects vacatur only where the vacating order is a member of this family. EO 3574 (Fort Davis) is decided by PLO 1712 on its own branch (P22).
Regex screens on the text decide that no reversion, retained right, redefinition or re-reservation is present; scan-OCR texts may hide such a clause.

BLM treated some Alaska transfers under the 1884 Act as continuing withdrawals: PLO 1712 (1958-08-07, held BLM table) revokes EO 3574 'entirely' and EO 7049 (four post cemeteries placed under Interior in 1935, on this branch) 'in part'. Under ruling P1 the transfer is spent on issue and the lead stands; if the owner reads such transfers as withdrawals pending disposal, Alaska members on this branch need the instrument that ended the withdrawal, and EO 7049's other tracts would be open.

Held later edges that act on the land after the order's date do not revive the spent act: EO 477 (1906) redefined the Fort Bayard reservation 'as modified by' EO 341-A; EO 5132 (1929) restored another parcel of the Hawaii Arsenal reservation that EO 3080 had also reduced; EO 4131 (1925) recites the Nulato right-of-way 'turned over to the Department of the Interior' by EO 3418. Each is flagged by the engine (acted_on_after_lead_end) and leaves the lead unchanged.

basis: A reservation for military, naval or departmental use stands until revoked, relinquished, transferred or disposed of. FLPMA sec. 701(c) kept every withdrawal and reservation in effect on October 21, 1976 in full force until modified, and sec. 704(a) repealed only the authority to make new ones; the Engle Act of 1958 is prospective. None of these ends or confirms a member. Many National Guard ranges were later revoked by executive orders or Public Land Orders; some reservations (for example the Fort Sill enlargement, EO 685) may still be military land. Members whose whole order a later instrument revokes by number or date are decided on branches C26-C30 and P01-P22.

A no needs the revoking order, Public Land Order, statute or surplus-property deed naming the order or its lands.

EO 2281 (Alabama military lands, 1915-12-06) carries held revocation edges from EO 5590 (1931), which revokes in part 'Executive order of December 6, 1915, creating Petroleum Reserve No. 40, Montana No. 1', a different order of the same date; the edge does not reach EO 2281. basis: The order opens returns to a named committee, official or class of officers (or generally under Treasury rules) and states no period or end. Its own terms tie it to the named body, whose end is not in the text; the 1976 rewrite of 26 U.S.C. 6103 does not name the order or describe a class of orders (P3), so it is only a candidate end.
gaps: Disclosed earlier candidate end: 1977-01-01, when Tax Reform Act of 1976 sec. 1202 (90 Stat. 1667, 1672, 1688; held) made returns confidential except as Title 26 authorizes and left no inspection upon order of the President; under P3 it does not end the member because it does not name it or an expressly described class that includes it.

For grants to a congressional committee under a resolution named in the text (EO 6241, 6712, 6742, 7039, 7097, 7115, 7158, 7322, 7350, 7411, 7483): the end of the committee's authority under its resolution, from the Journal or Congressional Record; a House resolution's authority ending with its Congress would need a held source (House rules or precedents).

EO 3595 (two firms' returns opened to 'Honorable Joseph W. Fordney, Chairman of the Ways & Means Committee', or a member he designates) and EO 6603A (returns opened to the House Committee on Naval Affairs) name no resolution: each grant runs to a standing committee, or its named chairman, and its end depends on that committee's inquiry or the chairman's tenure, which no held source fixes.

For general orders under Treasury rules and standing orders for State officers (EO 1999, 2882A, 2934A, 3212, 3624, 3971A, 4078, 4416, 4940, 5321, 5647, 5824, 5970, 2130): a later order that supersedes them by number or by express class.
TR-TAX-RETURN-INSPECTION was checked: no member's own text limits inspection to a stated period or date.

basis: A refuge reservation continues until revoked; renaming (1940) and transfer to Interior (1939) continue it; if the area was in the Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps it until Congress acts (subject to the statute's exceptions for acquired-land disposals, exchanges and cooperative agreements), and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) bars the Secretary from revoking a withdrawal that added lands to the System before October 21, 1976. Whether the order's lands were still reserved in 1975 is not shown by the fields held.
gaps: Needed: evidence that the order's area was in the Refuge System on or after 1975-01-01 (FWS Annual Report of Lands for 1975 and the current year, matched to the order by a reviewed crosswalk) or a PLO revoking it.

Several such orders were revoked in part by PLOs (EO 2446 by PLO 2291, EO 4519 by PLO 988, EO 7106 by PLO 4641 and amended by PLO 1511, EO 7489 by PLO 3385); a partial revocation leaves the order in force as amended.

A held edge on EO 923 (Key West Reservation, 1908) from EO 10383 (1952) is a misresolution: EO 10383 restores lands set aside by 'Executive Order No. 923 of January 30, 1941, of the Governor of the Territory of Hawaii', not this order.

basis: The order is an operative act on land whose forest designation persists, not a pure textual amendment, so ruling P2 does not reach it; it ends only when a later order or statute names it or expressly redescribes the forest's whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions, and no such instrument is held.
gaps: The Forest Service chronological record mapping this order to the named forest's later actions (consolidation, renaming, redescription), with the text of each later instrument to test whether it names this order or expressly redescribes the whole boundary while revoking prior descriptions.
For a persistence lead: the current Land Areas Report showing the forest or name on 2026-10-14. 16 U.S.C. 1609(a) is context only.

Where the forest the order constituted was later abolished or merged by name but the order also assigned land to another forest (for example EO 870, Holy Cross and Leadville, Holy Cross abolished by PLO 263; EO 801, Pocatello and Cache, Pocatello merged by EO 2179), ruling P7 does not reach it and the lead stays open.

basis: If the refuge was in the National Wildlife Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps the area in the System until Congress acts; but (a)(6) expressly does not preclude transfer or disposal of acquired lands under 668dd(a)(5) (which needs Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval), exchanges, or disposal under a cooperative agreement, and these orders reserve acquired lands. Needed: evidence that the order's acquired lands were not transferred, exchanged or disposed of under 668dd(a)(5), (b)(3) or a cooperative agreement, none of which needs an Act of Congress.
No held search shows a full revocation; absence of a found revocation is not evidence of persistence.

basis: A lighthouse reservation continues until revoked by order or PLO, or until the station is conveyed; the 1939 transfer of the Bureau of Lighthouses to the Coast Guard and transfers of jurisdiction (for example EO 6896 moving San Miguel and Prince Islands to the Navy) continue it. gaps: Two held later edges are flagged by the engine as ending edges on this persistence-kind open lead; neither is a full end: PLO 1724 (1958) revokes EO 431 ("EOs of ... Mar. 27, 1906") only "in part" per the BLM table; PLO 7391 (1999) revokes an Oregon power-site order of November 14, 1917 (Power Site Reserve No. 658), a date collision with EO 2755, not EO 2755 itself.

Search the BLM PLO tables (held) and Federal Register for a PLO naming the order by number or date; the 1867-1906 and Alaska multi-site orders (for example EO 4257, revoked in part by six PLOs 1960-1994) need site-by-site review.

Later held BLM headings show partial revocations only: PLO 7583 (2003) of the Ediz Hook Lighthouse Reservation (reduced by EO 2646), and PLO 7723 (2008) of lighthouse withdrawals for Channel Islands National Park, which may reach the San Miguel, Prince and Santa Barbara Island orders (EO 1066, 2750, 347B, 6896); which lands they released is not identified in a held copy.
Light stations conveyed under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act (2000) or surplus-property law end by deed; GSA and NPS conveyance lists are not held.

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
Machine-read or mirror text: a reviewer must confirm the operative clause against an authenticated copy.

basis: The member's own text only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; its text merged into those rules on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent rules were expressly revoked by EO 89 ('revokes all others') on May 6, 1896.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: The member's own text only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; its text merged into those rules on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent rules were expressly revoked by EO 89 ('revokes all others') on May 6, 1896.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: The member's own text only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; its text merged into those rules on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent rules were expressly revoked by EO 89 ('revokes all others') on May 6, 1896.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: The member's own text only amends the text of the civil service rules then in force; its text merged into those rules on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent rules were expressly revoked by EO 89 ('revokes all others') on May 6, 1896.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: The member's own text only amends the 1896 Civil Service Rules (EO 89); its text merged into EO 89 on issue and the amending order has no command of its own after that day (ruling P2). The parent EO 89 ended on April 15, 1903, when EO 209 took effect 'in lieu of those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof'.
gaps: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents). A pattern scan of all B12-B15 texts with this marker list was the measure of the test; an unmarked further provision in other words would still escape it

basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.
gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.

basis: Words that reach the reservation: section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directs the surrender of 'all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', states that the United States 'hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised' over the territory; and Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946) withdraws and surrenders all such rights 'except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases, and the right incident thereto, as the United States of America, by agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, may deem necessary to retain'. The agreement so made, the Military Bases Agreement in force March 26, 1947, retains the use of the bases listed in Annex A (and Annex B on necessity), which do not include this member's place; keeps the Port of Manila reservation (art. XXI(2)); and keeps only one other class outside the bases: 'temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases ... for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years', with any extension fixed by agreement, barred for the City of Manila, and one that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years' (art. XXI(1)). Member test: the reservation lies in the Philippine Islands, is an Army reservation, and its place is neither an Annex A or B base nor the Port of Manila reservation. Whether U.S. forces still occupied an installation on this member's land in 1947 is not known from the fields held; if they did, art. XXI(1) let them stay at most two years plus an extension of at most three years, so the U.S. right over the land ended no later than five years after the agreement took effect.

date.basis: No later than the outer limit of art. XXI(1) of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement: two years plus an extension that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years', counted from the agreement's entry into force on 1947-03-26 (on the narrower reading that three years is the whole period, 1950-03-26; for temporary installations within the City of Manila, where no extension was allowed, 1949-03-26). July 4, 1946 (Proclamation 2695) or October 22, 1946 (Treaty art. I) for a member whose land held no U.S. installation in 1947; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands.

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) and the Military Bases Agreement (61 Stat. 4019; 43 U.N.T.S. No. 673) are read on the web only; acquire them.

Note V of the 1947 agreement, in full: 'I have the honor to state, in signing the Agreement of March 14, 1947, Between the United States of America and the Republic of the Philippines Concerning Military Bases, the understanding of my Government that the question of the adjustment of any rights and titles held by the United States pursuant to the provisions of the Act of Congress of March 24, 1934 (48 Stat. 456) as amended, specifically Section 10(b) thereof, the Joint Resolution of the Congress of June 29, 1944, and the Act of Congress of July 3, 1946, and Treaties and Agreements heretofore entered into between the United States and the Philippines, to real property in any of the bases covered by the aforementioned Agreement or any naval reservations or fueling stations not so covered is reserved and will be settled subsequently in accordance with the terms of the Acts and Joint Resolution of the Congress mentioned above.' (61 Stat. 4033; Note VI, the Philippine reply, concurs 'without conceding the existence of any rights or titles to the real property therein referred to'.) Note V reserves title questions for the bases and for naval reservations outside them (the latter routed to B20n); it does not reserve the possession and control of an Army reservation outside the bases, which Article I surrendered. Section 5 of the 1934 Act likewise kept designated reservation lands out of the 1935 grant to the Commonwealth. Any U.S. title that outlasted the surrender is a property question disclosed here, not a continuation of the reservation.

The joint resolution of June 29, 1944 (58 Stat. 626) is read on the web only; which bases, if any, the President withheld under it before July 4, 1946 is not established in the sources held. A withheld base is retained only through the 1947 agreement, so the interval's bound covers it.

Which members' lands held U.S. temporary installations in March 1947 is not known; the interval's upper bound assumes the widest reading of art. XXI(1). A later agreement extending a temporary installation beyond the art. XXI(1) limit would be a new instrument; none is held.

For Manila members: Proclamation 2694 of July 3, 1946 (closing part on the held 60 Stat. 1352 page; number, title and authority read on the Truman Library copy; opening page not verified) designated nine Manila properties for U.S. diplomatic and consular establishments under section 10 of the 1934 Act as amended in 1939; any U.S. use of such a property rests on that proclamation, not on a military reservation order.

EO 1437 (Regan Barracks target range) was placed under the Government of the Philippine Islands by EO 3086 of 1919, 'subject to such reimbursement and reservations as may be prescribed by the Secretary of War'; because of that proviso the class interval is kept. EO 1628 (Fort Pikit and Fort Reina Regente) appears to have been transferred by EO 3056 of 1919-03-03 (see branch C28).

EO 985 carries a held 'amendment' edge from EO 10069 (1949), which amends 'Executive Order No. 985 of November 25, 1946' on travel expenses; that is a different order (a misprint of the number), so the edge does not act on EO 985. The engine flags it (acted_on_after_lead_end).

basis: Words that reach the reservation: section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directs the surrender of 'all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', states that the United States 'hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised' over the territory; and Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946) withdraws and surrenders all such rights 'except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases, and the right incident thereto, as the United States of America, by agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, may deem necessary to retain'. The agreement so made, the Military Bases Agreement in force March 26, 1947, retains the use of the bases listed in Annex A (and Annex B on necessity), which do not include this member's place; keeps the Port of Manila reservation (art. XXI(2)); and keeps only one other class outside the bases: 'temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases ... for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years', with any extension fixed by agreement, barred for the City of Manila, and one that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years' (art. XXI(1)). Member test: the reservation lies in the Philippine Islands, is an Army reservation, and its place is neither an Annex A or B base nor the Port of Manila reservation. Whether U.S. forces still occupied an installation on this member's land in 1947 is not known from the fields held; if they did, art. XXI(1) let them stay at most two years plus an extension of at most three years, so the U.S. right over the land ended no later than five years after the agreement took effect.

date.basis: No later than the outer limit of art. XXI(1) of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement: two years plus an extension that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years', counted from the agreement's entry into force on 1947-03-26 (on the narrower reading that three years is the whole period, 1950-03-26; for temporary installations within the City of Manila, where no extension was allowed, 1949-03-26). July 4, 1946 (Proclamation 2695) or October 22, 1946 (Treaty art. I) for a member whose land held no U.S. installation in 1947; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands.

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) and the Military Bases Agreement (61 Stat. 4019; 43 U.N.T.S. No. 673) are read on the web only; acquire them.

Note V of the 1947 agreement, in full: 'I have the honor to state, in signing the Agreement of March 14, 1947, Between the United States of America and the Republic of the Philippines Concerning Military Bases, the understanding of my Government that the question of the adjustment of any rights and titles held by the United States pursuant to the provisions of the Act of Congress of March 24, 1934 (48 Stat. 456) as amended, specifically Section 10(b) thereof, the Joint Resolution of the Congress of June 29, 1944, and the Act of Congress of July 3, 1946, and Treaties and Agreements heretofore entered into between the United States and the Philippines, to real property in any of the bases covered by the aforementioned Agreement or any naval reservations or fueling stations not so covered is reserved and will be settled subsequently in accordance with the terms of the Acts and Joint Resolution of the Congress mentioned above.' basis: Words that reach the reservation: section 10(a) of the Philippine Independence Act directs the surrender of 'all right of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty' over the Islands, 'including all military and other reservations of the Government of the United States in the Philippines (except such naval reservations and fueling stations as are reserved under section 5)'; Proclamation 2695 of July 4, 1946, 'subject to the reservations provided for in the applicable statutes', states that the United States 'hereby withdraws and surrenders all rights of possession, supervision, jurisdiction, control, or sovereignty now existing and exercised' over the territory; and Article I of the Treaty of General Relations (in force October 22, 1946) withdraws and surrenders all such rights 'except the use of such bases, necessary appurtenances to such bases, and the right incident thereto, as the United States of America, by agreement with the Republic of the Philippines, may deem necessary to retain'. The agreement so made, the Military Bases Agreement in force March 26, 1947, retains the use of the bases listed in Annex A (and Annex B on necessity), which do not include this member's place; keeps the Port of Manila reservation (art. XXI(2)); and keeps only one other class outside the bases: 'temporary quarters and installations now existing outside the bases ... for such reasonable time, not exceeding two years', with any extension fixed by agreement, barred for the City of Manila, and one that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years' (art. XXI(1)). Member test: the reservation lies in the Philippine Islands, is an Army reservation, and its place is neither an Annex A or B base nor the Port of Manila reservation. Whether U.S. forces still occupied an installation on this member's land in 1947 is not known from the fields held; if they did, art. XXI(1) let them stay at most two years plus an extension of at most three years, so the U.S. right over the land ended no later than five years after the agreement took effect.

date.basis: No later than the outer limit of art. XXI(1) of the 1947 Military Bases Agreement: two years plus an extension that 'shall in no case exceed a period of three years', counted from the agreement's entry into force on 1947-03-26 (on the narrower reading that three years is the whole period, 1950-03-26; for temporary installations within the City of Manila, where no extension was allowed, 1949-03-26). July 4, 1946 (Proclamation 2695) or October 22, 1946 (Treaty art. I) for a member whose land held no U.S. installation in 1947; earlier if a later order revoked or restored the lands.

gaps: The Treaty of General Relations (61 Stat. 1174) and the Military Bases Agreement (61 Stat. 4019; 43 U.N.T.S. No. 673) are read on the web only; acquire them.

Note V of the 1947 agreement, in full: 'I have the honor to state, in signing the Agreement of March 14, 1947, Between the United States of America and the Republic of the Philippines Concerning Military Bases, the understanding of my Government that the question of the adjustment of any rights and titles held by the United States pursuant to the provisions of the Act of Congress of March 24, 1934 (48 Stat. 456) as amended, specifically Section 10(b) thereof, the Joint Resolution of the Congress of June 29, 1944, and the Act of Congress of July 3, 1946, and Treaties and Agreements heretofore entered into between the United States and the Philippines, to real property in any of the bases covered by the aforementioned Agreement or any naval reservations or fueling stations not so covered is reserved and will be settled subsequently in accordance with the terms of the Acts and Joint Resolution of the Congress mentioned above.' (61 Stat. 4033; Note VI, the Philippine reply, concurs 'without conceding the existence of any rights or titles to the real property therein referred to'.) Note V reserves title questions for the bases and for naval reservations outside them (the latter routed to B20n); it does not reserve the possession and control of an Army reservation outside the bases, which Article I surrendered. Section 5 of the 1934 Act likewise kept designated reservation lands out of the 1935 grant to the Commonwealth. Any U.S. title that outlasted the surrender is a property question disclosed here, not a continuation of the reservation.

The joint resolution of June 29, 1944 (58 Stat. 626) is read on the web only; which bases, if any, the President withheld under it before July 4, 1946 is not established in the sources held. A withheld base is retained only through the 1947 agreement, so the interval's bound covers it.

Which members' lands held U.S. temporary installations in March 1947 is not known; the interval's upper bound assumes the widest reading of art. XXI(1). A later agreement extending a temporary installation beyond the art. XXI(1) limit would be a new instrument; none is held.

For Manila members: Proclamation 2694 of July 3, 1946 (closing part on the held 60 Stat. 1352 page; number, title and authority read on the Truman Library copy; opening page not verified) designated nine Manila properties for U.S. diplomatic and consular establishments under section 10 of the 1934 Act as amended in 1939; any U.S. use of such a property rests on that proclamation, not on a military reservation order.

EO 1437 (Regan Barracks target range) was placed under the Government of the Philippine Islands by EO 3086 of 1919, 'subject to such reimbursement and reservations as may be prescribed by the Secretary of War'; because of that proviso the class interval is kept. EO 1628 (Fort Pikit and Fort Reina Regente) appears to have been transferred by EO 3056 of 1919-03-03 (see branch C28).

EO 985 carries a held 'amendment' edge from EO 10069 (1949), which amends 'Executive Order No. 985 of November 25, 1946' on travel expenses; that is a different order (a misprint of the number), so the edge does not act on EO 985. The engine flags it (acted_on_after_lead_end).

only-content test: the WPA summary shows nothing but an amendment (no waiver, special rule, promulgation, prescription, construction or extension); the member's operative text uses amending words in an operative form ('is hereby amended', 'strike out', 'by adding', 'to read as follows'; title words such as 'Amending' do not count); and the text has none of the markers of a further provision (present or continued incumbents or occupants, persons now holding, serving or employed, 'it is further ordered', 'the effect of this amendment', status given to persons, a saving for incumbents).
